notes: The transitional input identity is a documented bhyve compatibility extension and is not part of the modern VirtIO 1.4 profile
The historical transitional vsock identity is selected explicitly and remains separate from the modern device identity
Packed rings are standard but their default-off release policy and per-device selection knob are implementation policy
The kernel provider ABI is a FreeBSD host contract rather than a VirtIO guest interface
The Unix-socket backend protocol is private to bhyve and its provider rather than an AF_VSOCK wire extension
The common VirtIO checkpoint envelope is a bhyve ABI, rejects obsolete versions, and never changes the guest-visible VirtIO wire format
Checkpoint metadata and member digests are private migration contracts rather than VirtIO configuration
Administration queues and device groups stay unadvertised until production topology and live qualification exist
Provisional modern devices are created only by an explicit device configuration and advertise only implemented standard features
Quiesce and backend timeout values are host availability policy and must not be mistaken for standard device timing
DTrace stages expose bounded identifiers and state transitions without becoming a guest or checkpoint ABI
The provider count is an operational observation and must not be used as transport ownership or synchronization
Balloon target, statistics interval, deflate-on-OOM, free-page reporting, page poisoning, and packed-ring selection are documented host policy knobs rather than new guest-visible features
The fixed-width little-endian balloon record preserves PFN ownership and negotiated optional state without serializing pointers, locks, timers, or guest queue ownership

Desired and current expose the specification-defined 4096-byte balloon units while poisoned is a saturating count of native VM pages initialized after acknowledged deflation; none is an ownership or synchronization interface

The writable alarm deadline and read-only notification evidence are FreeBSD management policy layered over standard RTC requests; request serialization, timeout, detach, and interrupt wakeups share one mutex so a policy write cannot lose completion or teardown wakeups

The explicit child-to-parent teardown boundary is a FreeBSD bus-lifecycle contract rather than a guest-visible VirtIO feature; it closes interrupt callbacks before any child lock, queue callback argument, or softc-owned handler state is destroyed

The FreeBSD SCMI transport locator and callback registration API is not a guest-visible VirtIO interface; singleton publication is serialized, get and put hold device lifetime, callback removal waits until no callback retains the consumer private pointer, every failed enqueue returns its unconsumed PDU to the bounded pool, and cleanup resets and drains the queues before freeing consumer-owned P2A buffers
The bhyve PCI transport record is fixed-width private migration state, rejects obsolete versions, and is separate from the VirtIO PCI capability layout visible to guests
Network queue cursors RSS state and backend identity use a bhyve record rather than a VirtIO wire extension, and obsolete versions are rejected
Block state rejects obsolete versions and changed media identity and never serializes host descriptors or worker objects
SCSI state records portable queue and LUN identity while CTL handles remain destination-local; malformed, truncated, or locally incompatible input is rejected before the external backend is consulted
Console state excludes host file descriptors and reconstructs port backends under the lifecycle transaction
The only accepted 9P checkpoint record binds the export contract without changing the guest 9P protocol; the unreleased version-1 layout is neither emitted nor accepted
Input state preserves only portable staged events and resynchronization metadata and rejects obsolete version-1 records
Userspace and kernel host backends share one private record but retain distinct reconstruction validation
GPU PCI and resource-graph subrecords reject obsolete versions, are private migration formats, and exclude host mappings
Virtio-fs request wire format remains standard while backend session reconstruction is bhyve-private
Guest memory-block state is portable while destination mappings and host allocation objects are reconstructed, and obsolete device records are rejected
Persistent-memory backing identity and range are a private checkpoint contract
Active host audio descriptors, PCM buffers, and callbacks are never serialized; a quiescent RUNNING stream is reconstructed as RUNNING only after destination lifecycle callbacks succeed
The private state record preserves standard IOMMU semantics but is not an administration or request-queue wire format
Host clock and alarm reconstruction policy is carried outside the standard RTC request protocol and obsolete device records are rejected
Unadvertised administration work has separately bounded private subrecords and must not become guest-visible merely because its checkpoint format exists

AF_VSOCK socket buffer sizing is FreeBSD resource policy rather than a VirtIO credit field; writers are serialized and values outside the complete cross-field invariant are rejected before publication

Guest CID connection counts traffic counters drops and PCB snapshots are host observability interfaces; pcblist emits bounded versioned records without conferring ownership or exposing kernel pointers

The incomplete-record fragment ceiling bounds host mbuf ownership independently of the standard VirtIO transport credit counters; zero explicitly removes the ceiling and each update is published atomically under the connection mutex

The global and per-CID PCB ceilings are FreeBSD resource policy rather than VirtIO wire limits; the source-level kernel harness independently covers inbound outbound and loopback admission rejection exact two-slot loopback reservation and immediate slot reclamation

Version-3 SHA-256 values detect accidental or post-publication member changes but are unkeyed integrity metadata rather than authentication; every non-current header is rejected as malformed before restore publication and no historical decoder exists

The fixed software FIFO and its sixteen-slot control margin are FreeBSD driver resource policy rather than VirtIO queue sizes; completed RX buffers remain device-owned at high water and are delivered exactly once after TX progress while detach drains every retained packet; last-resort drops increment kern.vsock.tx_drops and fire the metadata-only vsock:::pkt-tx-drop probe

The /dev/vsock userspace-provider packet ceilings are FreeBSD host resource policy rather than VirtIO credit or virtqueue fields; the final slot is reserved for a synchronous control reply and one provider cannot backpressure a distinct CID

The userspace backend bounds one VM device to 256 transport connections and 16 host control clients; independent literal assertions pin the operational policy while exact-cap overflow and reclamation tests prove existing connections remain live

The queue and pending-operation ceilings bound host allocation and backend pressure rather than extending the VirtIO-fs wire protocol; the test pins both private literals and rejects zero and above-limit queue configurations

The production IOMMU table sizes are bhyve resource policy and are not standard domain or address-space maxima; independent literal assertions bind the configured state object while focused state tests exercise capacity failure and recovery with smaller tables

The input backend caps one host-staged event frame at 4096 events; the test pins the private value, exercises exact saturation, and separate delivery tests prove the next complete frame reports loss without publishing a truncated frame

The RNG backend services at most 65536 bytes from one descriptor chain; this is host latency and resource policy rather than a standard request-size maximum, and the independent test pins the literal while proving bounded completion
The net backend processes at most 256 descriptors per packet path; the test pins that private ceiling independently while standard maximum packet length remains derived from the specification fixture
The common block backend reserves one request element per advertised ring slot plus one per worker; independent literals distinguish this host scheduling policy from device queue-size negotiation

The checkpoint topology record supports at most eight NUMA domains; the test pins the private value and validates exact vCPU and memory partitions so future architecture support must version or deliberately raise the format policy

The SCMI transport polling cadence is FreeBSD scheduling policy rather than a VirtIO wire requirement; poll mode may execute where sleeping is forbidden, so it uses bounded DELAY calls, rounds a positive sub-interval timeout to one probe, and must accept a target reply on the final probe

The provider management timeout bounds RESET FREEZE and SET_FEATURES while in-flight copyin or copyout crosses the domain mutex; all three operations close read write and AF_VSOCK packet admission before draining so continuous traffic cannot replace each completion, direct reads and writes observe the same frozen fence, and a pre-commit failure restores an independently active outer checkpoint fence

PCI and MMIO selective queue reset cannot sleep because callers may hold a child mutex; both use 1000 delays plus an initial and final probe, so completion exactly at the private one-second deadline succeeds instead of being reported as timed out

PCI and MMIO guest transports use the same bounded sleepable lifecycle policy; each iteration observes status before applying the deadline so completion on the final wakeup is not lost, while NEEDS_RESET or FAILED takes precedence over timeout

GPU and RTC control requests plus balloon inflate or deflate requests use private bounded waits; wakeups cannot renew a deadline indefinitely, and timeout enters each driver's ownership-revocation path
The guest SCSI driver caps request virtqueues at 64 after validating the device count; the value bounds kernel allocation and does not constrain the device configuration ABI
The standard supplies event_info_size but does not require unbounded guest allocation; FreeBSD accepts valid event records through one MiB and posts four receive buffers

The guest block driver bounds queue allocation at 64 and gives the complete suspend drain one absolute 30-second deadline; individual completions cannot renew that deadline. A busdma callback owns a request outside every software and VirtIO queue, so both suspend and detach include its explicit BUSDMA_WAIT predicate; detach closes callback admission and waits without a deadline because freeing the DMA tag or mutex while that retained callback exists is unsafe
The guest console driver caps the device-supplied port count at 32 before allocating two queues per port plus control queues
The guest input driver owns fixed event and status slot arrays; their sizes bound posted DMA buffers independently of the device queue maximum
The basic guest GPU driver supports one enabled 2D scanout and caps its framebuffer allocation at 256 MiB after checked stride and size arithmetic

The guest balloon driver batches 256 standard PFN entries per request; this follows common implementation practice but remains FreeBSD scheduling and allocation policy rather than a normative batch size
The 9P guest transport converts zero to a one-second minimum and saturates very large values; spurious wakeups cannot complete an unmatched response or renew the request deadline

Full reset is intentionally not converted into a timeout because the current void transport API has no safe failure result and child drivers may immediately free queue DMA; a noncompliant device can therefore stall detach, and replacing this policy requires a fallible ownership-revocation API rather than an unsafe deadline
The guest network driver has private fairness, memory, watchdog, filter, and queue ceilings; they remain distinct from the standard 32768-pair wire maximum and device-advertised configuration
The synchronous 9P guest transport allocates a 20-segment software sglist; this bounds physical fragmentation accepted for one request without changing the negotiated 9P message size
Console input is posted and consumed in 128-byte chunks and control messages use a separate 128-byte allocation; compile-time assertions keep both within one page and fit the standard config record
FreeBSD caps an indirect descriptor table at one native page, so the operational ceiling varies by architecture page size; this must not be serialized or treated as a cross-architecture guest ABI

The connect default and timeval socket option intentionally follow Linux observable behavior; the close deadline is local reclamation policy for an unread peer shutdown and neither duration is a VirtIO wire timeout

A failed host-page allocation delays the next inflate attempt by one second; the delay is a replaceable scheduling hint and remains separate from the five-second absolute device-request ownership deadline
FreeBSD allocates ten extra request objects for non-normal command paths after applying its 64-request-virtqueue cap; this reserve is kernel resource policy and is not advertised to the device

Module unload intentionally waits without a deadline because open descriptors can still call TTY methods in module text; a bounded failure would require a fallible unload contract rather than freeing live ports or unloading their callbacks
hw.virtio.pci.disable_msix and hw.virtio.pci.transitional are FreeBSD boot policy; they select among standard transport and interrupt modes and are not feature bits or device configuration
hw.vtblk.no_ident, global and per-device writecache_mode, the runtime writecache_mode sysctl, and num_queues are FreeBSD management surfaces layered over standard block features
hw.vtscsi.bus_reset_disable, per-device debug level, active queue count, and request counters are FreeBSD operational policy rather than VirtIO SCSI configuration
The nvqs, host_features, and negotiated_features nodes describe the current FreeBSD attachment and must not be used as synchronization or as an oracle for standard constants
The per-device p9fs_mount_tag node exposes the validated mount tag for operators; malformed device configuration fails before the channel or sysctl is published

The architecture-neutral container is the sole current STRUCT_VM representation. It separates common and architecture-specific typed sections, matches common and architecture state by sparse vCPU instance, and preserves zero-active-vCPU images. Production save stages the exact sparse common and amd64 set with one TSC sample; production restore rejects unknown critical records and all semantic, topology, and event-owner inconsistencies before any destination state changes, then publishes through a transactional all-vCPU restore plan under the ingress lease. The removed native-order stream is neither selected nor accepted as a decoder fallback.

PCI and modern MMIO use the same independently tested status classifier and rollback order; the bhyve device accepts cumulative driver FAILED while suspended, while a live rebuilt-5BSD lane remains required to inject timeout, NEEDS_RESET, child-resume failure, and completion-boundary races

The crash-dump path cannot depend on scheduler-driven interrupts or allocate recovery state, so it intentionally polls without a host deadline. A device which withholds completion can stall that dump, but imposing a timeout would only abandon device-owned DMA and cannot make the destination dump complete; this policy is isolated from ordinary attach, suspend, and I/O waits

alarm_time_ns is a FreeBSD management mapping for the negotiated ALARM feature, not device configuration; zero issues SET_ALARM_ENABLED with disabled state while retaining the device deadline as specified, and alarm_count plus alarm_observed_time_ns are observational rather than synchronization interfaces

The session reuses the machine-independent event coordinator rather than adding an architecture or device-specific lock. ABORT_CURRENT exists only because an IOWR BEGIN can acquire the descriptor owner before failing its identity copyout; it cannot target another descriptor and rejects a nonzero identity. Destination publication is protected from concurrent event ingress but deliberately does not claim rollback of already replaced memory or external backend effects; a failed destination remains stopped.

The event callback compares its exact softc identity before recycling a completion; a non-NULL global owner is not enough because a replacement must never receive notification or rearm work through the retired queue.
Administration command support is a provisional host topology contract.  Restore rejects a destination which has a different command mask instead of silently accepting an unimplemented command.

Capability-manager state is private provisional administration machinery.  A missing, reordered, size-mismatched, or invalid destination capability is unsupported rather than a compatibility fallback.
Device-part commands require a registered private member handler and an exactly compatible destination resource contract; no partially implemented part becomes guest-visible.
The administration group fabric is withheld until a concrete ownership topology exists.  Restore rejects a changed group set rather than manufacturing a destination membership.
Administration queue-bank dimensions are private retained state and must match exactly on restore; the provisional interface never silently truncates command buffers or queue identities.
Resource-manager reconstruction is private provisional infrastructure.  Unknown resource types, object IDs, dependencies, or changed limits are unsupported and leave the destination fabric unchanged.
The device-parts envelope is a private provisional codec.  Its optional-bit skip rule does not advertise an administration feature and required unknown parts fail closed.
The virtio-fs backend control protocol is a private host ABI.  State-changing control commands require their negotiated backend feature before session publication.
Backend state transfer is private checkpoint transport.  A backend without the required negotiated features cannot be treated as checkpoint-capable.

The private VFSB notification frame carries an unsolicited FUSE notification after backend capability negotiation. It uses request ID zero, a nonzero active incarnation, zero status, and one nonempty bounded payload. The connection retains at most one consumed notification while no guest notification buffer exists; the next queue-one kick retries delivery without polling. This private backpressure policy must not be confused with the standard VirtIO queue layout or device feature bit.
Cancellation is a private backend capability, not an implicit FUSE behavior.  It fails closed before changing accepted-request ownership when the backend did not negotiate it.
The queue converts an unavailable backend cancellation operation to a retryable reset fence; it never claims a destructive reset completed while an accepted request remains backend-owned.
The bounded 2D engine recognizes only its advertised command subset.  Optional GPU commands are not accepted merely because their common control header is syntactically valid.
The internal ENOTSUP result is never exposed as a host errno to the guest; the queue maps it to the documented GPU response after preserving queue ownership.
The IOMMU parser distinguishes bounded unknown requests from malformed supported requests.  This subset policy remains provisional until live ACCESS_PLATFORM qualification completes.
The request executor implements the specification-permitted unknown-request consumption behavior while keeping unsupported operations out of the advertised IOMMU feature contract.

The filesystem backend uses bounded absolute waits only with CLOCK_MONOTONIC condition attributes.  This is a private host operational contract, not a guest-visible VirtIO feature, and prevents wall-clock adjustments from changing checkpoint timing.

The persistent-memory worker uses an event-driven, bounded monotonic drain for reset, suspend, and destroy.  This private host lifecycle policy must not depend on wall-clock time or reopen admission before the last durable-backing owner retires.

The host block reset drain uses one monotonic absolute deadline and keeps stale callbacks discard-only on timeout.  This private lifecycle policy prevents host wall-clock changes from altering ownership fencing.

The provisional administration owner deliberately uses an unbounded predicate wait during destruction: a command already dispatched may retain its handler argument, so no deadline can safely free the owner.  The interface remains unadvertised until a real topology can provide a complete standard administration lifecycle.

The entropy device deliberately has no private snapshot callback or device configuration payload.  Common transport and queue state are retained, while the destination opens and uses its own host entropy source so a checkpoint cannot replay entropy bytes.

The private filesystem connection drains retained guest requests during destruction.  Its queue pointer is unpublished before callbacks run because completion telemetry may query pending or outgoing pressure while ownership is retired.  A destroying latch makes callback-side mutable operations fail with ECANCELED, preventing a callback from activating a replacement queue while the old queue is being reclaimed.  The caller serializes concurrent public operations and excludes destroy from every connection call; a synchronous completion callback may submit only on that same serialized path and may not destroy the connection.

The provisional GPU presentation callbacks deliberately execute outside the state mutex so a display owner can query presentation state.  Destruction first prevents new commands, retains the state through every callback already admitted, and drains that set before releasing callback storage, resource memory, or synchronization primitives.

VirtIO-IOMMU state has a deliberately owner-managed raw-pointer lifetime.  Its external GPA-map and fault callbacks run outside the state lock, so a local reference count cannot make a stale caller safe.  The device owner must unpublish state, stop request admission, and drain every common DMA lease before freeing it; validation views follow the same unpublished-before-destroy rule.

The private sound backend progress callback may inspect the async owner, so it executes without the async mutex.  A per-stream progress pin preserves job and payload ownership; cancellation, lifecycle quiesce, and destruction reject until that callback returns and the owner safely completes or retains the job.

VirtIO-memory platform callbacks run outside the state and operation mutexes so they may safely perform host memory work or query configuration.  A separate public-operation lifetime fence prevents destroy from reclaiming the model or callback argument until every admitted callback has returned.

The synchronous sound host invokes selected backend operations under operation_mutex.  Destruction takes that same lock before releasing synchronization or callback storage, so a slow backend callback cannot race its final stream-state publication with host reclamation.

The RTC timer event callback dereferences the PCI softc.  Any initialization rollback after event installation must wait for callback retirement and close the timer descriptor before freeing the alarm model or softc; the shared mevent synchronous close-delete operation supplies that exact boundary.

Userspace-vsock child callbacks carry a private event reference containing the device softc.  Initialization rollback first publishes the lifecycle pause and detaches both connection lists while holding the device mutex, then retires every child event synchronously outside that mutex before the softc can be reclaimed.  Normal event-thread connection teardown remains asynchronous and identity-checked because it cannot synchronously wait for itself.

The console driver uses synchronous control and tty-output commands whose descriptors reference caller-owned stack storage.  One monotonic five-second deadline bounds each command without renewal; a missing or malformed completion resets the device and reclaims the descriptor before that storage can escape, preventing a nonresponsive device from freezing boot or a tty caller indefinitely.

VT drawing callbacks execute from the display timer while critical context may be active, so they may only update framebuffer memory, merge an exclusive-edge damage rectangle under a spin mutex, and enqueue through a spin-protected queue.  A dedicated taskqueue kernel thread owns synchronous transfer and flush commands.  VT deallocation precedes task draining and thread termination, which precede framebuffer and lock reclamation, closing late-enqueue, active-worker, and global sleep-mutex races.

The crypto checkpoint record is a private versioned ABI: a mismatched magic or version is rejected as unsupported before any state is consumed, a destination whose data-queue count or session-table geometry differs from device creation cannot restore it, and live session counts are recomputed from the decoded table rather than trusted from the wire
